contribution: Development of empirical methods for industrial organization, specifically structural estimation of demand and market equilibrium with differentiated products (the BLP approach), which underpins modern analysis of competition, mergers and market power
rationale: This is a low-confidence guess. Recent prizes went to growth, institutions, labor and finance, while empirical IO has never been recognized, even though BLP-style demand estimation is foundational for antitrust and policy evaluation. Pakes is the most likely laureate, with Berry and Levinsohn as co-developers. Trade with heterogeneous firms (Melitz and Helpman) is a plausible alternative.
